## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D3. This is audit backlog UX-30 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Staff, audit log, formulary, order sets (compact allowed); every other table (controller, paging, stacked rows).
Findings and reviewers: F-24 · reviewers C-06, C-13.
Rationale: Staff rows are about 69 px (7 per screen); the audit table starts 800 px down a 4,192 px page; 2 of 19 tables can be sorted; 10 rely on sideways scrolling on phones, which can hide dose or identity columns.
Proposed UX behaviour: A shared table controller hook for sort, filter and paging state (the pattern AGENTS.md section 4 already asks for), adopted one table at a time, audit log and staff first. Sort on the columns people sort by (name, time, wait). Paging above 50 rows. Under 768 px a table becomes stacked rows and never scrolls sideways with hidden columns that carry dose or identity. Numbers right-aligned with tabular numerals; the identifying cell bold and nothing else; one visible row action, the rest in a menu. Compact density (36 px rows) is an explicit per-table prop allowed only on the audit log, formulary, order sets and staff list; it is ignored on any device that reports a coarse pointer (any-pointer: coarse), and a destructive action inside a compact table (Offboard, Remove) stays 44 px or asks to confirm. AGENTS.md section 4 is amended in the same change, as the house rule requires for any row under 44 px.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md sections 4 and 9.
Components and tokens affected: table.tsx (density prop, stacked variant), a table controller in web/clinic/src/features/table, pagination. Density tokens.
Front end and back end split: Front end only. Server paging only where a list is already paged.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the library-defaults and token tickets. Timing: after the first pilot weeks, or before the first staff training session if the founder moves it there; never between training and the first two pilot weeks (arbitration ruling 6).
Clinical sign-off: Question 20 of the validation plan (mouse or touch at the desk and in the office) informs it. Compact on any clinical list would need clinical sign-off and is not in scope.
Effort and regression risk: L · Medium: many tables; one table per pull request.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Compact density on the patient directory, patient pickers, medicine lines, the front-desk list or any row that changes state (forbidden by ruling 2). (2) Virtual scrolling. (3) New table features nobody asked for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given the density prop, when it is set on a table other than audit log, formulary, order sets or staff, then the build or lint fails
- [ ] **AC2.** Given a compact table on a device with a coarse pointer, when it renders, then rows are 48 px
- [ ] **AC3.** Given the audit log at 1440 by 900 with a mouse, when it opens, then at least 15 rows are visible and the table starts in the first 300 px
- [ ] **AC4.** Given staff and audit log, when a sortable header is used by keyboard, then the order changes, the sort state is announced, and lists over 50 rows are paged
- [ ] **AC5.** Given any table at 375 px, when it renders, then there is no sideways scrolling and no dose or identity field is hidden
- [ ] **AC6.** Given Offboard in the compact staff table, when it is measured, then it is at least 44 px or opens a confirmation
- [ ] **AC7.** Given AGENTS.md section 4, when this change merges, then it names the four tables and the coarse-pointer rule
- [ ] **AC8.** Given English and Arabic, when axe runs on each migrated table, then there is no violation and every scrollable region has a label

## Test notes

- Vitest: controller hook.
- Playwright: staff.spec.ts, audit-log.spec.ts, formulary.spec.ts with sort, paging and 375 stacked rows; a coarse-pointer emulation check.
